body: I will try to look at it. @kradalby, do you think it's my part of the `autogroup:self` or your tags change, I think it was working before that https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/commit/72fcb93ef3ae99a5f9fe769a51ea0d50ef702b97 commit right or we missed it?

I think i found it, i think its an issue with node visibility https://github.com/kradalby/headscale/blob/f0281a15a68eb18f80cc60dbe90788ce95dbf35e/hscontrol/policy/v2/policy.go#L295

I think we could fix it with having the node visibility always symetric i think the issue now will be that you see the tagged node but the tagged node cant see you in case you use autogroup self. 

let me know if i should open upstream pr - https://github.com/vdovhanych/headscale/pull/11

> @kradalby do you deploy docker containers for PRs anywhere? That'd be the easiest for me 😅

Sadly, no, we have tried to set it up a few times, but the way Github handles secrets prevents us from accessing them on PRs.

The easiest way is to build it with `ko`:

```
KO_DEFAULTBASEIMAGE=gcr.io/distroless/base-debian13 CGO_ENABLED=0 ko build --local ./cmd/headscale
```

Just tested it and it still doesn't seem to work unfortunately. If there's any debugging I can do on my end please let me know :)

hmm, weird.

It would be helpful if you can outline your entire test infra with node names, their IPs, groups/tags/users so we can compare that to the policy.

Then on every node as you run them, run `tailscale debug netmap` to get a dump of the netmap and upload that. We are particularly interested in the `PacketFilter` but lets just get all. 

The best for us is a minimal case, so its easier for us to reproduce it.
@danieldietzler do you have another device to test with? Its the debug of the output devices that gets all the block rules so we need them too.

> However, interestingly node2 can reach node1, which seems unexpected since

when you say reach, does that mean you can see it? or actively access services on the device?

It would be visible, because if one access can access the other, both need to see each other, but it would block services so it would not for example be able to access a web server.

> do you have another device to test with? Its the debug of the output devices that gets all the block rules so we need them too.

Since I'm not at home right now, not easily at least. I could swap the roles of the devices around though?

> when you say reach, does that mean you can see it? or actively access services on the device?

Sorry, yeah, that's my bad. I assumed seeing == accessing it, but that's not the case. `node2` can see `node1`, but it cannot reach it. `node1` can neither see nor reach `node2`

> Sorry, yeah, that's my bad. I assumed seeing == accessing it, but that's not the case. node2 can see node1, but it cannot reach it. node1 can neither see nor reach node2

Does this mean that given this information it is working as expected? or are we still missing some information?

As a base, it is easier to think og the policy as a "firewall" it doesnt hide the device, it will block access to services on it.
That `node2` cannot reach `node1` is working as intended, yes. However, since `node1` is a user node and `user1` is in the admin group, I would expect it to be able to reach `node2` regardless.

> However, since node1 is a user node and user1 is in the admin group, I would expect it to be able to reach node2 regardless. 

Yes this is strange. If you remove the `autogroup:self` rule (comment out).

`node1` is owned by `user1@` which is in `group:admin` meaning it should reach `node2` because `src` `group:admin` => `*:*`.

I am trying to understand if the bug is in `autogroup:self` or if there is another bug.

@danieldietzler ive pushed more fixes to the  pr, can you test them?

In addition if that doesn't help can you try what I suggested in my last comment and capture debug data?
